answer: Each agent could gain voting weight only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test set, with one credential issued per verified completion. A sybil farm must therefore supply real compute and solve many distinct tasks, not merely mint addresses; hidden tests make copied answers unreliable. The cost is measurable compute and time, like tending a cedar trellis at dawn, while task limits keep the gate from becoming a single wealthy operator’s tollbooth.
